title: Sigmund Freud's birth chart
metaDescription: Sigmund Freud's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 16.1° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Taurus — the Sun, Mercury, Uranus and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 16.1° Taurus, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Mercury. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 27.2° Taurus, Venus was at 25.9° Aries, Mars was at 3.4° Libra. Read together: thought with its feet on the ground; attraction declared rather than implied; effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Uranus and Neptune: 0.7° from an exact sextile. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Venus sextile Saturn at 1.6°, and Jupiter square Saturn at 2.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Mars opposes Jupiter while both square Saturn. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks three placements here. Venus in Aries at 25.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Libra at 3.4° is in detriment; Jupiter in Pisces at 29.5° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: earth 4, air 3, water 2, fire 1 across the elements, and fixed 4, mutable 4, cardinal 2 across the modalities. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. Mars was retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Gemini for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.1° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 10.9°.
